choices.text: They do not: respiration stops when the light goes out
Respiration runs all the time, day and night, to release energy from food
They only start respiring once photosynthesis has finished for the year

questions.feedback: That trap answer is the one to unlearn: Only animals breathe; plants do not. Reteach point: Plants take in and give out gases too: they respire all the time, day and night, just like us. Check scene s4: gases move in and out of the leaf in the day and at night as well.
questions.misconception: Only animals breathe; plants do not.
questions.prompt: Why do plants respire at night, when there is no light for photosynthesis?

questions.answer: Light plus water plus carbon dioxide become food plus oxygen.
questions.feedback: Scene s2 fixes the recipe: sunlight, water from the roots and carbon dioxide from the air arrive at the leaf, and food and oxygen come out.
questions.prompt: State the photosynthesis recipe in one sentence.

questions.feedback: Scene s1 fixes the picture: the roots grow below the soil and drink in water at the root tips, while the leaf catches light and the stem holds the plant up.
questions.prompt: Which part of the plant drinks in water from the soil?

questions.answer: Respiration breaks down food and oxygen to release energy, making carbon dioxide and water - the opposite direction from photosynthesis.
questions.feedback: Scene s3 fixes the idea: photosynthesis builds food and oxygen from light, water and carbon dioxide, while respiration breaks food and oxygen back down, releasing energy.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, say how respiration is the reverse of photosynthesis.
